question: How can parents protect their children from sexual abuse?
answer:
Dear parents, this was a very difficult topic merely to talk about. I'm going to be honest with you: I have no doubt that many of you just turned off in the middle of the Q&A and just said, "I don't want to listen to this." Some people don't have the luxury of turning off the memories that happened to them. If you had the luxury to turn this video off and just walk away, thank Allah. Thank Allah.

But realize, there are statistics that are harrowing, that are shocking. Here in America, it is estimated that roughly one out of four girls is sexually abused. And for boys, the statistics vary, but the one that I read, one out of ten (some say one out of fourteen) boys will be sexually abused. We're talking about sexual; we're not talking about physical abuse or whatnot. That's bad in its own way. Sexual abuse compounds the problem. Sexual abuse is the worst type you can do to a young child, a'udhu billah. And one out of four, a'udhu billah, a'udhu billah.

And I know I'm going to get into a lot of trouble. I ask Allah's forgiveness and protection. I want to say that (Allahu al-musta'an, it's difficult to even say these types of things), but I am fairly confident that that statistic is higher in our cultures than it is outside of our cultures. I ask Allah's forgiveness if I'm wrong. I ask Allah's forgiveness if I've gone overboard. But anecdotally, I have taught not tens of thousands, actually hundreds of thousands of Muslims, alhamdulillah, through the classes I've done, personally, one-on-one. And throughout those classes, throughout interacting with people from across this country, in the Western world, the number of stories that you hear... And in some classes, when I was teaching a particular topic, I actually did an anonymous survey, and the statistics amongst the females was more than one out of four.

Now, I'm not a trained psychiatrist, so you can put all the caveats: it's anecdotal, etc., etc. But I think I'm fairly confident in stating that in our cultures, for whatever reason (and this is a fault of our cultures, a'udhu billah, not of our religion; our religion is perfect, but we are human), in our cultures, I feel that the statistic is higher than one out of four.

Be that as it may, even one out of four... Wallahi, even one out of one hundred is bad enough, but one out of four, do you understand what that means? Out of four girls, one is being abused. How can we turn a blind eye? How can we ignore? How can we make this topic taboo? For the love of God and the love of our children, let's talk about this publicly. Let's talk about this clearly. We do not want this to happen to a single child, much less one out of three or one out of four, much less in our own communities and our own masajid, a'udhu billah.

And one thing I haven't even brought up yet, because again, there's so much to talk about (it's not because it's taboo, for me at least), and that is the abuse of the clergy. In this particular case, the sister's email is the abuse of an uncle. Okay, that's bad; that's very bad. And what is also very bad, which is unfortunately also common: sometimes it's the Qur'an teacher, sometimes it's the clergyman, the person whom you trusted because he's supposed to be a man of God, and he ends up doing this to your child, a'udhu billah, a'udhu billah. And that ends up a whole different problem. And that problem is this young man or woman then grows up hating the faith, because a man who was supposed to be the man of the faith was the one who did this to him or her.

And then you want me to be quiet about this? You want us to act as if it's embarrassing, as if we're going to cover up? A'udhu billah, somebody has got to be blunt, and somebody has got to just say this loudly and clearly: we need to talk about the rampant sexual abuse that is within our own cultures and societies. Sometimes by the elders, sometimes by the men that are supposed to be Qur'an teachers, sometimes by the men that are supposed to be the men of faith, and we seek Allah's refuge from all such evil.

A'udhu billah. Listen, dear brothers and sisters, all of us are sinners. I'm a sinner, you're a sinner. But there's a special category of sinners that we should have zero sympathy for, and that is those that are perpetrating sexual violence against children. A'udhu billah, I have zero sympathy, zero, for somebody that will abuse his position, either as an elder or as a family member or as a religious person, to then do something of this nature. A'udhu billah, a'udhu billah. So, dear brothers and sisters, enough is enough. I apologize for getting emotional, but wallahi, it's just something that needs to be said. And I hope, inshallah, if I've said anything wrong, I ask for Allah's forgiveness in this regard.

But I'm saying in my conclusions here that these statistics are unbelievable. And whether they're worse or not in our societies or cultures, they are bad enough. One out of four, I mean, it is mind-boggling. One out of four, wallahi, it is mind-boggling. A'udhu billah.

So the statistic that, again, I want to also share with you: the majority of this abuse, the majority of it, occurs from people that the family knows. And this is another unbelievable statistic. The most prominent organization that is researching sexual abuse in North America, they released a survey (was it two years ago?): **93% of abusers are known to their victims.** 93%! 7% strangers; 7%, somebody that you have no idea about, and that's okay, 7%. You cannot protect against the complete unknowns. 93% of abuse is from family and friends. Let that seep in. Around 35% are from immediate family members, of that 93%, and around 60%, roughly, less than 60%, is from friends. So one out of three is from immediate family, and almost two out of three, a little bit less than two out of three, is from friends.

Now, where does one begin with this as well? We all say, "No, no, no, not my family and friends, not my... that's not my..." Dear brothers and sisters, one out of four, statistically. Statistically, does that protect you and me? One out of four. How many children do you have? How many sons and daughters do you have? And again, abuse is rampant amongst girls and boys. Yes, more girls, but also boys; it happens too much. Even one out of 12 is bad enough for boys, one out of 10; one out of four for girls; 93% from immediate family and friends.

Now, I'm not telling you to now start doubting your own siblings and your own... Come on, we shouldn't have... But I'm telling you to take precautions. I'm telling you to be wise. I'm telling you to be reasonable. I'm telling you to not be naive, and to get your head out of the sand: "Oh, it's not going to happen anywhere." Dear Muslims, it's rampant in our societies and cultures. One out of four, that's rampant. Do not think that it can never happen. I ask protection for my daughters and for your daughters (I have daughters too; I will ask protection for them), but you cannot be naive. This is a reality of our communities and of the world around us. So I'm not asking you to double guess any friend that comes, or any family member. I'm asking you to be reasonable and to err on the side of caution.

What can be done? Again, this is a whole different topic, but some basic things. And by the way, even the Prophet, what advice did he give? Such beautiful advice. And this is in a society where this was not a common thing in that society. But our Prophet said that when children reach the age of 10 years old, make them separate in the beds. Don't let the girls... And this is when they had one room for all the kids, or they're all sleeping together. Our Prophet ﷺ said, make the boys one place, the girls another place, in the same room. In our times, if you're able to put them in different rooms, excellent. They're siblings, but Shaytan comes at night. Shaytan comes in the privacy when nobody's there. So sometimes a person might not even know that he's capable of this thing, but all alone at night, or this or that, nobody's watching, Shaytan takes over him. So don't give that opportunity.

So what can be done? Some generic advice. Of the things that you parents should do is to teach your children. Teach your children about haya, about safety protocols. Even from the age of two or three, tell them about body parts and what's private. Use names that they'll understand. You don't have to use technical medical terms. Use names that are funny for them; they'll understand. Teach them: Adam and Hawa came down and Allah dressed them, right? Haya: teach them modesty. Teach them some parts are private. Tell them very clearly, in different conversations, that there are no secrets from Mommy and Daddy, from whatever you call yourselves, Ami, Abu: there's no secrets from us. Anybody who comes to you, anybody who comes to you and says, "Don't tell Mommy, don't tell Daddy," just tell them: "No, you have to come to us. Always come to us."

Also, dear parents, generally speaking, generally speaking, a young child cannot invent lies about this topic. Cannot. A four-year-old? I mean, I'm not going to say impossible, but come on. Who are you going to believe? An elder that's going to deny, or a four- or five-year-old child that's saying things that are just not... And you can tell the nature of the child. A child, by nature, when a child feels uncomfortable around an adult... Allah has created us with such purity that children know something is wrong. Children know. And then you should be able to sense that something is wrong when this adult... And again, don't read in too much when it's not there, but don't be naive. And this is the problem. Don't be suspicious of everybody, but don't be trusting of everybody either, right? Be somewhere in the middle here. Be wise. Set your rules.

And I'll be very honest here, dear parents; let me speak to you as a parent to a parent. Because of who I am, and because of all the horror stories that have come my way since beginning my preaching and teaching, I have been ultra strict with my own children. My boys are now older, so their time is gone. My girls are still in the younger stage. And I have a very hard and fast rule that we never allowed them to stay over the night at anybody else's house unless it was one gender. Like, they have female cousins, and only the females are there; I let my girls go there. Otherwise, no. And again, this is my own; not that I have any doubts, but just because... why? And again, this is not Islamic advice, by the way. This is parent to parent. This is my own routine. I'm not forcing it on you. But for me, I would err on the side of caution.

My point being, dear parents, that after all that you have heard, of these statistics, of the story, of the trauma that is caused, subhanAllah, just don't give this opportunity. Even the smallest percentage of a chance of happening, just shut it as much as you can. Take as many reasonable precautions as you can. And don't allow your children to be alone for extended periods of time with anybody, even whether it's a Qur'an teacher, whether it's anybody. Have some area of public: if a person's coming to teach or something, in the living room, with the distance between them.

And again, I'm not asking you to doubt all Qur'an teachers. I had a Qur'an teacher as well as a child. Alhamdulillah, he was a great man. He taught me Qur'an. Alhamdulillah, may Allah bless and forgive him. Alhamdulillah, we all had Qur'an teachers, my children too, so please don't misunderstand. May Allah forgive if sometimes my wording was a little bit harsher or whatnot, but wallahi, it's out of protection. It's out of wanting to err on the side of protection and caution for our children.

And then the final point, for those who perpetrate or are thinking of perpetrating such violence: fear Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, and fear the day that that innocent child and soul will be able to speak in front of the throne of Allah, and you will have nowhere to hide. You will have nowhere to hide on that day. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala will call you to task for each and every harm that you have caused. And in that trial there is no defense, because your own skin will testify against you.

May Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala protect all of our children. May Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala grant all of us safety and security. May Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala bless all of us to that which He loves.
